text_blocks.snippet: A "tax degree" typically refers to a Master of Science in Taxation (MST) or a Master of Accounting with a concentration in Taxation. These degrees prepare individuals for careers in tax accounting, consulting, and compliance, often within public accounting firms, corporations, or government agencies. While a background in accounting is common, a tax degree can also be pursued by those with business or finance backgrounds.
snippet_highlighted_words: typically refers to a Master of Science in Taxation (MST) or a Master of Accounting with a concentration in Taxation

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of a tax degree:

list.title: Curriculum:
list.snippet: MST programs focus on specialized taxation skills and regulations, including corporate, federal, and partnership taxes. They delve into advanced tax topics, tax research, and ethical considerations.

list.title: Career Paths:
list.snippet: Graduates can pursue roles such as tax consultant, auditor, IRS agent, tax manager, or specialist in various industries.

list.title: CPA Licensure:
list.snippet: While an MST doesn't automatically qualify graduates for CPA licensure, it can be a valuable stepping stone. Some programs, like the one at Baruch College, offer courses that can be applied towards the 150-hour requirement for CPA licensure.

list.title: Master of Accounting (Taxation Concentration):
list.snippet: Some universities offer a Master of Accounting with a specialization in Taxation. This option provides a broader accounting foundation while still offering in-depth tax knowledge.

list.title: Loyola Law School's Tax LLM:
list.snippet: For those interested in tax law, Loyola Law School offers a Tax LLM (Master of Laws) program. This advanced degree is designed for lawyers and focuses on the legal aspects of taxation.
